title: Trump Ally Laura Loomer Allegedly Pocketed Thousands for Undisclosed Political Posts
snippet: Far-right activist Laura Loomer reportedly collected up to $5,000 per post on social media to push hidden political agendas, highlighting a shadowy online influence market.
content:
Prominent right-wing activist and staunch Donald Trump ally Laura Loomer has reportedly been quietly collecting thousands of dollars to publish political content on her social media channels without disclosing the financial backing to her nearly two million followers.

According to campaign insiders and financial documents reviewed by news outlets, Loomer charged between $3,000 and $5,000—and sometimes more—per post on X (formerly Twitter). Bank transaction records and wire transfer statements indicate that a Florida-based firm tied to Loomer, King Breaker Media, received more than $60,000 in payments starting in mid-2023. Alex Bruesewitz, a top adviser to Trump’s 2024 campaign, publicly confirmed paying Loomer through his political consulting agency for issue-based posts.

Under the Influence of Unchecked Messaging

Loomer vehemently denied the allegations, insisting she is a public affairs strategist and opposition researcher rather than a paid social media influencer. She claimed payments from consulting firms were strictly for underlying research documents, not sponsored tweets. Shortly after being questioned about the financial arrangements, Loomer announced a hiatus from her digital show, "Loomer Unleashed," citing a need for personal time.

The controversy highlights a growing, largely unregulated sector of digital politics. While the Federal Trade Commission enforces strict rules requiring influencers to disclose paid product endorsements, political commentary operates in a murky legal gray area. Ethics groups and researchers warn that undisclosed paid messaging damages public trust and misleads voters about organic online support.

Despite the backlash, Loomer remains an influential voice within MAGA circles, known for her direct line to the former president. A source familiar with her strategy described her powerful, unpredictable reach as a double-edged sword: highly effective for getting a message across, but volatile if unmanaged.
